findings.message: Instance fix of the round-1 'pin keyed on a name' finding (R3/059). ThisWeek and SheetPage now pin project rows by `projectId`, but this file is in the diff and was missed. The project rows of My timesheet still pin `get_timesheet { week, project: <name> }`, and `getTimesheet` resolves that by a name match. `MyRow` carries no project id, so the page can't pass one. Fix: add `projectId` to `MyRow` in my.ts and pin `{ week: m.key, projectId }`. Extend pin-by-id.test.ts to cover the own-week path.
findings.scenario: Kasun pins his 'Fleet Tracker, 2026-W42' row on My timesheet. A PM renames the project to 'Fleet Tracker Pro'. The pin's `get_timesheet { week: '2026-W42', project: 'Fleet Tracker' }` now matches no row, so the pinned record resolves to an empty or wrong row instead of the renamed project.

findings.message: `onProjects` now reads allocations through `listAllocations`, which returns `{ rows, hidden }`, and keeps only `rows`. People the reader's HR scope can't see are dropped without a trace. The code treats them as 'not allocated', so 'could not see' reads as 'nothing there'. Before this change the raw SQL counted them. `expectedBy`, which feeds Not started, remind_missing and utilisation, now leaves them out with no signal. Fix: surface `hidden` (for example, a 'N people on your projects could not be checked' note on the card or grid), or resolve a manager's own projects through a contract read that is scoped to project management rather than HR visibility.
findings.scenario: Maya manages Fleet Tracker. Dinesh is allocated to FLT for October but has logged no time, and Maya's HR scope doesn't include him. remind_missing for 2026-10-20 neither lists nor skips Dinesh. Team time's Not started doesn't show him, and nothing says one person couldn't be checked.

findings.message: `mayAddOn` is a second rule for the same question `mayFix` and `mayMove` answer: may this viewer put the owner's hours on project P in a locked week? The two can disagree. `mayFix` lets in anyone with `time:log` scoped to the owner in their entity; `mayAddOn` lets in only the owner's direct manager who also approves in that entity. Applying a 'move to P' request and an 'add on P' request therefore get different answers for the same viewer, owner and project. Fix: derive one predicate from the other (for example, `mayAddOn = (v, owner, p, e) => mayFix(v, owner, p, e)` plus the manager clause, if the manager clause is the intended rule for both). Use it from mayMove too.
findings.scenario: A viewer holds `time:log` over Kasun in his entity but not `time:approve` on HR Insights, and is not Kasun's line manager. They can apply Kasun's request to move an entry to HR Insights, because mayFix allows it. They are refused when they apply Kasun's request to add 1 h on HR Insights, because mayAddOn rejects it.

findings.message: The id-keyed pin is still found through a name lookup: `find((p) => p.name === n)?.id`, with rows grouped by name. `getTimesheet` then turns the id back into a name and filters by that name. Rows for two projects shown as 'Closed project' (or two projects with the same name) merge into one row whose pin carries only the first id. A closed project's id is also missing from `projectNames`, so its pin resolves to null. Fix: group the rows and filter `getTimesheet` by project id end to end.
findings.scenario: Kasun has hours on two closed projects in W42. Team grid shows one 'Closed project' row that sums both. Its pin carries one id, and `getTimesheet` returns null for it because `projectNames` has no closed projects.

findings.message: This real-date test copies the one in `workDay` (the comment says so). It now lives in two places that can drift apart. Fix: export one `isRealDate(day)` helper from week.ts and call it from both.

The new `mayAddOn` docblock was inserted between the existing 070 docblock and the function that docblock describes (`mayMove`). The 070 comment about moving entries now sits detached above another function's doc. Fix: move the 070 docblock back directly above `mayMove`.

This is an instance fix of the 'pin keyed on a name' finding. `get_timesheet` takes `projectId`, but it turns the id back into the project's current name and filters by name again: `own` uses `r.projectName === project`, and `projectRow` uses `e.projectName === project`. That happens even though `EntryLine` now carries `projectId`. A name is not unique. `projectNames` (`listProjectRefs`) also returns only active projects, so the id of a closed project's row resolves to null even though the row is on the page. SheetPage also gets the pin's id by name (`cells.flatMap(...).find((p) => p.name === n)`), so rows that share a name get the first project's id. Filter entries and rows by `projectId` all the way through, and group SheetPage rows by id, not by name.
findings.scenario: (1) Two active projects are both named 'Platform' (keys PLA and PLB), and Kasun logs on both. Pinning the PLA row returns PLA and PLB hours together. (2) Fleet Tracker is closed after week 42. Its row on Kasun's W42 sheet (shown as 'Closed project') pins `projectId=<FLT id>`, and get_timesheet returns null because the id is not in the active-only name map.

findings.message: Two of this round's fixes ship without a test that drives them. (1) The B3 fix removes `.catch(() => ({ done: null }))` from `claimChoice`, but no test makes `claimKey` fail and asserts the confirm surfaces an error instead of a `not_chosen`/cancelled decision. (2) The B10 blocker fix in `expected.ts` (reads through the allocations and HR contracts) has no test showing that allocated-but-not-logged people are still expected for `expectedBy` and `expectedIn`. Add a table-driven test for each that fails without the fix.
findings.scenario: Put back `.catch(() => ({ done: null }))` in claimChoice, or the raw `allocations.allocation join hr.person` query in onProjects, and every test in the diff stays green.
